# Empty-cell AutoFit writing minimum

Original deterministic OOXML is generated by
`tools/autofit_writing_minimum_fixture.py`. The two six-page packages use
compatibility modes 12 and 15. Each contains 24 single-cell automatic tables:
Arial/Calibri paragraph marks, 4/10/24/72pt sizes, and 0/80/160-twip side
margins. Both the grid and cell preference are one twip. No font files or
third-party document content are included.

The reference application opened each exact package read-only and repaginated it.
`tools/record-native-cell-widths.ps1` recorded `Cell.Width` in points and source
hashes in the accompanying JSON. Every case requires the combined margins plus
six twips (0.30pt), independent of font, size and compatibility mode. The prior
one-pixel writing minimum added fifteen twips instead, overstating the empty
cell's minimum by 0.45pt. `mode15-native.pdf` is an additional six-page visual
reference exported with `tools/export-reference.ps1`; widths are asserted
against the cell API, not PDF fill bounds.

The engine uses the six-twip minimum in its existing content, grapheme and
padding-floor constraints. Actual measured text/image widths still override
that minimum. Content-only weights exclude the empty writing allowance as
before. This introduces no new measurement pass, cache or content loop.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.87 permits different AutoFit algorithms and describes
minimum/maximum content widths and proportional reductions. §§17.4.42 and
17.4.68 specify cell margins; §17.4.71 specifies preferred cell widths. The
six-twip reserve is observed reference compatibility, not a normative requirement
or a demonstrated contradiction of the specification.

The browser regression compares all 48 widths within 0.01pt, edits the first
empty cell into an M, verifies growth without changing the other 23 widths,
checks unrelated package parts, exact undo, and editable export/reopen. It
explicitly skips when either reference font is absent. Existing legacy
crossing-span PDF comparisons now pass at their unchanged 0.2pt tolerance.
Modern crossing-span allocation still has separate unresolved differences.

Validation: 85 relevant unit checks (one existing picture-package assertion
requires a 30-second command-level timeout on this machine on both unchanged
main and the candidate), 24 browser scenarios including four existing expected
failures, schema checks, and production build/license gate. All six modern
native/app page pairs were inspected. This does not certify every AutoFit
combination or resolve the newsletter's unavailable Avenir font.
